from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, finite mapping-complex adjunction infrastructure through lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints and lem-coef-small-saturated-arrow-accessibility; HTT Lemma 5.5.4.13, Corollary 5.3.4.14 (printed p. 401), Proposition 2.1.2.1 (printed p. 60), Proposition 3.3.4.5 (printed pp. 219-220), and the relative lifting construction in the proof of Lemma 5.5.4.13 (printed pp. 479-480)

title: Relative finite-stage factorization of compact coherent cocones
statement:
Use the universes, $\kappa$-smallness, $\kappa$-filteredness and $\kappa$-compactness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], the coherent diagrams and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the join $\star$ and right cone $K^{\triangleright}=K\star\Delta^0$ of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe and let $\mathcal E$ be a locally small quasicategory admitting all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Let $K'\subseteq K$ be a simplicial subset of a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and $q:K\to\mathcal E$ a diagram with $\kappa$-compact values at all vertices. Let $I$ be a small nonempty partially ordered set in which every subset of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has an upper bound, and let $\bar p:N(I)^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ be a colimiting cocone with apex $c$ at its final vertex $\infty$. Here a cocone $\bar p:N(I)^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ is colimiting when its induced coherent cocone, obtained by precomposition with the map $N(I)\times\Delta^1\to N(I)^{\triangleright}$ that keeps the initial $N(I)$-vertices of each interval simplex and sends its final vertices to the cone vertex, is a colimiting cocone of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Suppose that
$$r:K'\star N(I)^{\triangleright}\longrightarrow\mathcal E$$
restricts to $q|_{K'}$ on $K'$ and to $\bar p$ on $N(I)^{\triangleright}$. Suppose also that $u:K\star\{\infty\}\to\mathcal E$ restricts to $q$ on $K$, has apex $c$, and agrees with $r$ on $K'\star\{\infty\}$. Then there exist $i\in I$ and a simplicial map
$$v:K\star\Delta^1\longrightarrow\mathcal E$$
with the following exact restrictions. On $K$ it is $q$; on $K\star\{1\}$ it is $u$, identifying $1$ with $\infty$; on $\Delta^1$ it is the edge $\bar p(i\to\infty)$; and on $K'\star\Delta^1$ it is $r\circ(\mathrm{id}_{K'}\star\iota_i)$, where $\iota_i:\Delta^1\to N(I)^{\triangleright}$ is the edge $i\to\infty$. No colimit of $q$ or $q|_{K'}$ is assumed to exist.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14 (printed p. 401), Proposition 2.1.2.1 (printed p. 60), Proposition 3.3.4.5 (printed pp. 219-220), and the relative lifting construction in the proof of Lemma 5.5.4.13 (printed pp. 479-480); read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent infinity-category result.

proof.text: Put $B=N(I)^{\triangleright}$. This is the nerve of the poset obtained by adjoining a new greatest element $\infty$ to $I$: a simplex in either description is exactly a chain with an initial block in $I$ and a final block at $\infty$. The nerve $N(I)$ is a quasicategory: an inner horn in dimension two specifies $i_0\leq i_1\leq i_2$, and transitivity supplies its missing edge; in dimensions at least three every adjacent edge is already in the horn, so the chain on the given vertices is the filler. All supplied faces agree with it because a poset simplex is determined by its ordered vertices. The nerve $N(I)$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Indeed, a map from a $\kappa$-small simplicial set $A$ has fewer than $\kappa$ vertex images. Choose an upper bound $j$ for those images. On each simplex the order arrows from its vertex images to $j$ define the extension to $A\star\{j\}$; uniqueness of a chain with fixed ordered vertices makes these extensions agree on all faces and degeneracies. Precomposing with $A\times\Delta^1\to A^{\triangleright}$ gives the required coherent cocone. For $A=\varnothing$, use nonemptiness of $I$. Thus the given induced cocone of $\bar p$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of the required kind.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, the filtered poset used in the relative construction; elementary nerve check; source read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: For $q'=q|_{K'}$, form the join coslices $\mathcal E_{q/}$ and $\mathcal E_{q'/}$ of [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration], working in a containing universe in which $\mathcal E$ is small. Specialize that node to the inner fibration $\mathcal E\to\Delta^0$ and the inclusion $K_0=K'\subseteq K$; all coslices of the terminal target are terminal, so its map $\rho$ is exactly $\mathcal E_{q/}\to\mathcal E_{q'/}$. Specializing instead to $K_0=\varnothing$ gives the absolute projections to $\mathcal E$, since the empty-diagram coslice is $\mathcal E$ degreewise. Pull back their projections along $\bar p:B\to\mathcal E$, and write $X=B\times_{\mathcal E}\mathcal E_{q/}$ and $X'=B\times_{\mathcal E}\mathcal E_{q'/}$. The projections to $B$ and the restriction $f:X\to X'$ are left fibrations: the first two are base changes of the coslice projections, and the third is a base change of coslice restriction. A horn lifting problem in a pullback is solved in its original fibration with the prescribed base simplex, and the pair gives a lift in the pullback. Under [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] their classified diagrams are the restrictions of $G_q,G_{q'}$ along $\bar p$. Both are colimit diagrams of spaces by [lem-coef-compact-diagram-cocone-transport] and Step 1. Its hypotheses hold for $K'$ as well as $K$: a simplicial subset has no more nondegenerate simplices, and its vertex values are among the compact values of $q$. Denote these two classified diagrams on $B$ by $G,G'$.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14 and Lemma 5.5.4.13, the two left fibrations X and X prime; source read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: The map $r:K'\star B\to\mathcal E$ is exactly a section $s:B\to X'$: on an $m$-simplex $\sigma$ of $B$ its coslice component is $r\circ(\operatorname{id}_{K'}\star\sigma)$. These components respect simplicial operators by precomposition. Define the strict pullback $Y=B\times_{s,X',f}X$. By [lem-coef-left-fibration-section-homotopy-pullback], its projection to $B$ is a left fibration and its classified diagram $H$ is naturally the pointwise homotopy pullback $G\times^h_{G'}1_B$. The comparison preserves the actual maps and restrictions. The given $u$ is a vertex $y_\infty$ of $Y$ over $\infty$: its restriction to $K'$ is exactly $s(\infty)$ by the agreement assumption, and its apex is the prescribed $c$. Thus the strict, rather than merely up-to-equivalence, fiber contains the required vertex.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, displayed pullback Y and the specified vertex v over the cone point; source read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text:
The span shape $\{a\to d\leftarrow b\}$ has three vertices and two nondegenerate edges, hence is $\kappa$-small even when $\kappa=\aleph_0$. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] to this shape and $N(I)$, using the coherent span $G\to G'\leftarrow1_B$ from Step 3. The empty-shape clause of that same lemma identifies the filtered colimit of terminal spaces with a terminal space. Steps 2 and 3 therefore give the canonical comparison
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}H(i)\simeq (\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}G(i))\times^h_{\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}G'(i)}(\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}*)\simeq G(\infty)\times^h_{G'(\infty)}*\simeq H(\infty).$$
Every map in this comparison is induced by the original cocone maps, the restriction $f$ and the section $s$; the naturality in Step 3 shows that its legs are the legs of $H$. Hence the actual induced coherent cocone of $H:B\to\mathcal S$ is colimiting. Apply the spaces lemma in a containing universe for these spaces; $I$ and $\kappa$ remain small there, so no larger indexing category is introduced.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, the assertion that the pullback Y is classified by a colimit diagram; filtered homotopy-pullback interchange expanded; source read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: By [lem-coef-left-fibration-colimit-realization] applied to $Y\to B$ and the colimit diagram $H$ of Step 4, the inclusion $Y_0=Y\times_B N(I)\hookrightarrow Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. In particular it is surjective on path components of realizations. Choose a point of $|Y_0|$ whose image is in the component of $y_\infty$, then choose a vertex $y_0$ of a simplex representing that point; the straight segment inside that simplex joins the point to $y_0$. The vertices $y_0,y_\infty$ are joined by a finite zigzag of edges of $Y$. To see the last assertion without replacing an edge by an unspecified homotopy, partition vertices by the equivalence relation generated by unoriented edges. Every simplex has all vertices in one class, and each such class gives an open-and-closed union of whole simplex summands in the quotient description of realization. Thus a continuous path cannot change class. Membership in the generated relation is precisely a finite edge zigzag. Since $y_0\in Y_0$, its base is a vertex $i\in I$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.5 and Lemma 5.5.4.13, printed p. 480; component-to-edge-zigzag argument written explicitly; source read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: Compress this finite zigzag into an incoming edge to the specified vertex $y_\infty$, using only the horn lifting property of the left fibration $Y\to B$ from Step 3. Work backwards from its final vertex, starting with the degenerate edge of $y_\infty$. If a zigzag edge is $a\to b$ and an edge $b\to y_\infty$ has been constructed, lift the horn $\Lambda^2_1$ on those two edges to get $a\to y_\infty$. If the zigzag edge instead is $b\to a$, lift the horn $\Lambda^2_0$ consisting of $b\to a$ and $b\to y_\infty$ to obtain $a\to y_\infty$. The base triangles exist exactly: $B$ is the nerve of a poset with greatest element $\infty$, so use the chain of the given edge followed by the unique arrow to $\infty$. Both horn indices $0,1$ are permitted for a left fibration in dimension two. Induction on the finite zigzag gives a single edge $e:y_0\to y_\infty$ over the unique edge $i\to\infty$. Its target remains the original vertex throughout.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, the incoming edge e; elementary two-dimensional horn construction made explicit; source read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text:
By the degreewise definition of the coslice, the $X$-component of $e$ is a map $v:K\star\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ with $v|_K=q$. The face at $1$ is the coslice component of its target $y_\infty$, so $v|_{K\star\{1\}}=u$ exactly. Its restriction to $\Delta^1$ is its base edge under $\bar p$, hence is $\bar p(i\to\infty)$. Finally the equality defining the simplicial pullback $Y$ says that the image of the entire edge $e$ in $X'$ is $s(i\to\infty)$. By the explicit section formula of Step 3, this equality is precisely
$$v|_{K'\star\Delta^1}=r\circ(\operatorname{id}_{K'}\star\iota_i).$$
These are all the required restrictions, with the original $q$, $u$, $r$ and $\bar p$. No colimit of $q$ or $q'$ was formed.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.13, printed p. 480, decoding the edge as the required relative extension; source read online, not archived in literature/

proof_origin.place: HTT Corollary 5.3.4.14 and relative construction in Lemma 5.5.4.13, pp. 479-480, read online; unarchived source. Agent expansion of filtered homotopy-pullback stability, components and exact horn-lift edge extraction.
